items.evidence: Header states "the FRUS Explorer corpus (552 volumes, 316,839 documents)" and §4 reports "314,676 of 316,839 documents carry a parsed date (99.3%) ... but 2,163 documents are undated and fall out of every by-decade figure here"; §2 adds "Per-decade tagging coverage of the corpus runs 60%–86% (1890s 60%, 1940s 78%, 1960s 86%)". I re-ran these against frus-copy.db: volumes=552, docs=316,839, dated=314,676 — exact. Coverage was measured over the index and reported.

The deliverable is framed as conditional throughout and the volume count is named: "Re: what the FRUS Explorer corpus (552 volumes, 316,839 documents) holds on this question"; §4 is headed "What the corpus cannot tell you, and you should know before you rely on it"; "appears in 18 documents in the entire 552-volume corpus"; §6(d) "every claim here comes from the SQLite index and the bundled JSON".

Documents are cited in volume/document form: "The earliest opium document in the corpus is 1861-12-24 (`frus1862/d669`, arms-and-opium trading)"; §5 lists "`frus1881/d133`, `frus1881/message-of-the-president` ... `frus1882/d76` (Frelinghuysen circular, April 1882), `frus1888p1/d200`, `d213`" and "FRUS 1946 vol. I (`d70`, `d96`, `d102`, `d320`, `d508`)". No claim rests on a title alone.

The one reproducer in §6 joins on rowid: "FROM frus_documents f JOIN document_cache dc ON dc.rowid=f.rowid" — rowid is used to identify which document each FTS hit is. It was avoidable: `frus_documents` is an external-content FTS5 table that carries `document_id` and `volume_id` as UNINDEXED columns, and I reproduced the memo's 1,118 by selecting the pair straight off `frus_documents` with no rowid anywhere.

Every document-level join in the shown SQL uses the pair: "JOIN document_dates dd ON dd.volume_id=u.v AND dd.document_id=u.d", and the union CTE is built on "SELECT DISTINCT volume_id v, document_id d" from both axes. No join on document_id alone. (The separate rowid defect is scored at I2.)

The memo never states an inclusion policy for front matter, and front matter is silently inside its headline set: I ran the memo's own union against `document_cache` and the 1,118 pre-1970 documents comprise 1,107 ordinary documents, 5 editorial notes and 6 front-matter records. §5 even offers a front-matter record as a lead — "`frus1881/message-of-the-president`" — without flagging it. The nearest disclosure is §4's "Only 5 editorial notes pre-1970 mention narcotics" (which matches my count exactly), but it never says whether those 5 are in or out of the 1,118, and front matter is not mentioned anywhere in the memo.

Neither `summary_text` nor `note_text` appears anywhere in the memo (grep returns nothing), and the stated surfaces are elsewhere: §2 "FTS5 over `frus_documents.body_text` (porter-stemmed)" and §3.3 "`document_sources` preserves each printed document's file citation". Quoted prose is from the printed record (Arthur's 1881 message), not a generated summary.

`cross_references` is never queried or mentioned anywhere in the memo; its two axes are FTS over body_text and `document_subject_refs`, with `document_sources`/`volume_sources` for the archival section. No cross-reference work was done, so the is_broken filter never arose.

Stemming is named and worked with: §2 "FTS5 over `frus_documents.body_text` (porter-stemmed)" using `narcotic*`, and §5 item 3 turns it into an explicit method choice — "Institution names as phrases, not stems: `"opium advisory committee"`, `"permanent central opium board"` ... These separate regime-machinery documents from commodity documents cleanly."

Periodisation runs off `document_dates.date_iso` — "WHERE CAST(substr(dd.date_iso,1,4) AS INT) < 1970" — and §4 states "Dates are document dates, not volume years." `citation_era` is never referenced. Where the memo does name filing-schedule generations ("`341.9` | post-1949", "`SOC 11–5` | post-1963 subject-numeric") it is labelling which classification schedule a class belongs to, not reading a period out of the era column.

Every archival count in §3.3 is attributed to one channel and stated as such — "`document_sources` preserves each printed document's file citation ... Measured in the corpus:" followed by the class table — and the follow-ups in §5 name the same table and columns ("`document_sources.decimal_class LIKE '511.4%'`", "`document_sources.raw_text LIKE '%.114 Narcotics%'`"). `external_citations` is never queried, and no count mixes the two.

Exactly one number in the memo carries its SQL — the §6 reproducer for 1,118. The by-decade table (24 figures), the year-by-year series (35 figures), the eight subject document-frequencies, the §2 axis-agreement table (102/34/982/1,118), the §3.3 file-class table and the thirteen §4 name counts are all reported bare. The memo offers a template instead ("Reproduce any number with, e.g."), and gives two exact predicates in §5, but the work behind the great majority of reported numbers is not shown. (The header's claim that "every number has a query behind it" is a claim, not shown work.)

Proportions carry denominators throughout: "**Roughly 1,100 documents dated before 1970 touch narcotics**, out of 285,060 pre-1970 dated documents (**0.39%**)"; the §3.1 table prints "narcotics docs | all docs | rate" per decade with an instruction to "Read the **rate** column, not the count"; "314,676 of 316,839 documents carry a parsed date (99.3%)"; "Of those 269, 147 mention 'liquor' and only 8 mention narcotics or opium." I verified 285,060 and 316,839/314,676 against the database.

Absence claims are stated and paired with evidence that the same query does return rows: §1/§3.3 "State had no narcotics office before 1971 ... its lot file (Lot 77 D 120) appears in the corpus only in 1969–76 volumes" and "The S/NM files (Lot 77 D 120, Vance) and IO/T/HNP files (Lot 81 D 327) exist in the corpus only from 1969 forward" — I confirmed Lot 77 D 120 resolves in `document_sources` to frus1969-76ve03 and nothing earlier. Likewise "`341.9` appears in exactly one volume of 552" is reported beside its 13 documents (verified: 13 docs, 1 volume). §6(c) also reports a null re-check and grades it: "I re-ran with `smuggl|contraband|illicit traffic` and found nothing narcotics-related that the first pass had missed, but that is a weaker check than I would like."

Thin results are explicitly flagged as properties of the source base rather than of history: "Whatever the corpus says about State's role, it will systematically understate the Federal Bureau of Narcotics, and the absence of Anslinger is not evidence of his absence from the policy"; "**The coca/cocaine side is thin.** ... are not, on this evidence, well represented before 1970"; "**`341.9` appears in exactly one volume of 552** ... That is the sharpest single statement of how thin the mid-century coverage is"; and §2's caveat that tag coverage of 60–86% means "axis B under-counts everywhere".

No control — positive or negative — is run on the search instrument anywhere; the word does not appear in that sense in the memo. What the memo has instead is triangulation between two result sets (§2's "88% agreement between a stemmed word search and a human-assigned tag") and post-hoc characterisation of false positives (§3.4's five classes; the `811.114` Prohibition trap at "147 mention 'liquor' and only 8 mention narcotics or opium"). Those validate results, not the query path, and no probe with a known expected answer is run in the same pass to show the apparatus behaves.

The counting surface is stated for the corpus scans: §2 "**Axis A — lexical.** FTS5 over `frus_documents.body_text` (porter-stemmed)", and §6(d) closes the question explicitly — "I did not open the TEI XML at all; every claim here comes from the SQLite index and the bundled JSON, and the index's own parse of source notes is what I trusted for §3.3."

Variants are expanded and the split is reported. The match expression carries spellings and phrase variants — "narcotic* OR opium OR cocaine OR morphine OR heroin OR marihuana OR marijuana OR cannabis OR \"coca leaf\" OR \"coca leaves\"" — the eight subject terms are broken out with per-term document counts (Opium 1,016 / Narcotics 631 / Heroin 175 …), §4 reports thirteen per-phrase counts ("'opium advisory committee'/'advisory committee on traffic in opium' 66"), and §3.3 splits file-number spellings ("`893.114` (+ `893.114-N`, `893.114N`)"). The axis split itself is tabulated: A-only 102, B-only 34, both 982, union 1,118 — which I reproduced exactly (1,118).

§4 says which was used and what it costs: "**Dates are document dates, not volume years.** 314,676 of 316,839 documents carry a parsed date (99.3%), so the temporal cuts above are reliable, but 2,163 documents are undated and fall out of every by-decade figure here." The shown SQL confirms it: "JOIN document_dates dd ... WHERE CAST(substr(dd.date_iso,1,4) AS INT) < 1970".

No mention of second editions, Ed2 volumes, or duplicate folding anywhere in the memo (grep for 'ed2', 'second edition', 'duplicat' returns nothing), and the fold was not checked and dismissed either. It is not hypothetical here: the index holds frus1951-54IranEd2, frus1969-76ve15p2Ed2 and frus1977-80v09Ed2, and running the memo's own union shows frus1951-54IranEd2 contributing 2 documents to its headline 1,118 pre-1970 set.

§3.3 establishes provenance for the relevant documents from `document_sources`: "| `511.4*` | US participation in the opium conferences | **165** |", "| `893.114` (+ `893.114-N`, `893.114N`) | China — traffic in narcotics | 54 |", `812.114 Narcotics` for Mexico, `341.9` for the UN Commission, plus "`volume_sources` also names the relevant lot files directly, e.g. for FRUS 1961–63 v. XXV: `RG 59, IO Files: Lot 67 D 378 ...`". I verified 511.4* = 165 documents and 341.9 = 13 documents in one volume.

The footnote channel is never touched. `external_citations` is not mentioned or queried anywhere in the memo, and no passage asks where the editors' notes point; §3.3 is built entirely on where documents came from ("`document_sources` preserves each printed document's file citation"), and §4's only remark about notes is a count of editorial notes ("Only 5 editorial notes pre-1970 mention narcotics"), not an analysis of their citation targets. The memo did substantial archival work, so the item applies.

Each archival count is attributed to its named source and none are added together: §3.3 opens "`document_sources` preserves each printed document's file citation" before the class table, then separately "`volume_sources` also names the relevant lot files directly", and §5's follow-ups re-name the table and column each time ("`document_sources.decimal_class LIKE '511.4%'` (165 docs, 20 volumes)", "`document_sources.raw_text LIKE '%.114 Narcotics%'` — 58 documents"). No total combines channels.

"From the bundled `decimal-class-labels.json` (the 1910–1949 schedule), **subject suffix `.114` = 'Traffic in liquors and habit-forming drugs'**, and class 5 = 'Congresses and Conferences'." I opened the same file in /Applications/FRUS Explorer.app/Contents/Resources/ and it carries `"114": "Traffic in liquors and habit-forming drugs"` verbatim. §2 also reads `document-subject-index.json` for the eight subject vocabulary indices.

Concrete targets are named: "`RG 59, IO Files: Lot 67 D 378, Deputy Assistant Secretary Richard N. Gardner Files, 1961–65, Opium…` — a concrete archival lead", plus "The S/NM files (Lot 77 D 120, Vance) and IO/T/HNP files (Lot 81 D 327)" and specific file classes (`511.4*`, `893.114`, `341.9`, `892.53: Narcotics traffic in Thailand`). I confirmed Lot 77 D 120 resolves in `document_sources` (frus1969-76ve03).

a6.notes:
The rubric's table lists 25 rows (C1–C2, I1–I3, E1–E3, T1–T3, R1–R4, S1–S5, A1–A5) although the heading says 24; I scored all 25. Compliance = 18/24 = 0.75.

Verification: I re-ran the memo's headline query and it reproduces exactly (1,118). Corpus counts (552 volumes, 316,839 documents, 314,676 dated, 285,060 pre-1970 dated), the archival counts I could check (511.4* = 165, 811.114 = 269, 341.9 = 13 in one volume), the Anslinger count (18), the Lot 77 D 120 volume range, and the decimal-class-labels.json gloss for .114 all check out. The one numeric discrepancy I found is minor and in a forward-looking recommendation: §5 says 511.4* covers "20 volumes"; the database says 26.

The ARCHIVAL block — the block the rubric flags as the discriminating one — is 4/5 obeyed and genuinely substantive: a decimal-file axis worked out from a bundled artifact, named lots and record groups, and a measured trap (811.114 is Prohibition, not narcotics). The single archival failure is A2: the footnote channel (`external_citations`) is never opened, so the memo answers "where did these documents come from" and never "where do the editors point".

The six failures cluster in method hygiene rather than archival reach:
- R1: one SQL block for one number, against roughly eighty reported figures. The memo substitutes a reproducer template and a claim that "every number has a query behind it"; the claim is not shown work.
- E1: front matter is silently inside the headline set (6 records, verified) and never mentioned; editorial notes are counted (5, verified) but never declared in or out.
- S5: the Ed2 fold is neither handled nor dismissed, and it is live — frus1951-54IranEd2 contributes 2 documents to the 1,118.
- I2: the shown SQL joins `document_cache` on rowid. Avoidable — the FTS table exposes volume_id/document_id UNINDEXED, and I got the same 1,118 without touching rowid.
- S1: no control on the instrument. The memo validates results (two-axis agreement, five measured false-positive classes) but never runs a probe with a known expected answer. This was the closest call I made; I resolved it against the memo because a control is applied to the method, and the memo's checks are applied to its output.
- A2 as above.

Judgement calls worth flagging for adjudication: S1 (argued above), R3 (scored obeyed on the Lot 77 D 120 / 341.9 absence claims, which do pair a null with proof the query returns rows elsewhere — the §6(c) null re-check alone would have been too weak), and I3 (scored obeyed because every document-level join uses the pair; the rowid join is penalised once, at I2, rather than twice).

This is a careful and largely honest memo — its self-criticism section names four real weaknesses including the one that matters most ("I sampled rather than classified") — but the rubric measures shown work, and its reporting discipline is where it thins out.

items.evidence: §10 opens with the coverage query and its result: `sqlite3 "$DB" "select count(*), count(distinct volume_id) from document_cache;"   # 316839 / 552`, and the header reports it: "316,839 documents, 552 volumes". I re-ran it: returns 316839|552 exactly.

Header: "**Corpus:** local FRUS Explorer index — 316,839 documents, 552 volumes, plus the TEI XML the index was built from and the app's bundled reference JSON." Conditionality is stated repeatedly: §1 "a **1948–60 hole that is a hole in FRUS's selection, not in the archive**"; §8 "the pre-1970 narcotics material this corpus knows about"; §9 is a dedicated "Limits of this pass" section.

Documents are cited as volume + document id throughout: "`frus1887` d148", "`frus1908` d72 (`File No. 774/197A`…)", "`frus1906p1` d332", "`frus1961-63v25` d326", "(d336, d342…)". Verified in the DB: frus1908/d72 header is "The Secretary of State to Ambassador Reid" with source note "File No. 774/197A."; frus1887/d148 is "Mr. Bayard to Mr. Denby"; frus1906p1/d332 is "The Acting Secretary of State to Minister Rockhill" — all as described.

`grep -niE "rowid"` over the memo returns nothing. Every identifier reported is a (volume_id, document_id) pair or a class/file number; e.g. §10's queries select `volume_id,document_id` and never rowid.

Every join in §10 is on the pair: "left join document_dates d using(volume_id,document_id)" (measure a), "join document_dates d using(volume_id,document_id)" (measure b), and "left join n using(volume_id,document_id)" in the 811.114 trap query.

No count in the memo filters apparatus material — §10's queries hit `document_cache`/`frus_documents`/`document_dates` with no `is_front_matter`/`is_editorial_note` predicate, and the DB holds 8,468 editorial notes and 1,012 front-matter rows inside the 316,839 denominator, the 64,632 window and the 1,676 keyword hits. Front matter is never mentioned at all. The only disclosure is local and partial: §9 "Two documents in the 1961–63 chapter have no header or date row at all (d336, d342 — probably editorial notes or attachments); they are counted in the compilation total" — true (both are is_editorial_note=1) but it is a note about two rows, not a statement of the counting policy behind the headline figures.

`grep -niE "summary_text|note_text"` returns nothing. The one long quotation, in §5, is verifiably the document's own `source_note`, not user content: I read frus1961-63v25/d326 and its `source_note` column begins "Source: National Archives and Records Administration, RG 59, Central Files 1960–63, 341.9/1–1961. Official Use Only. Anslinger was Commissioner of Narcotics in the Department of the Treasury. The instructions were drafted on January 18 by Chester G. Dunham…" — word-for-word what the memo quotes. (It mislabels it "The FRUS editorial note", but the source is the printed note, not `note_text`.)

`grep -niE "cross_reference|is_broken"` returns nothing; the memo's four measures are FTS keywords, `document_subject_refs`, `volume_structures.structure_json` and `document_sources`. It never uses the cross-reference table, so the exclusion never arose.

The counting surface is named with its tokenizer in the §2(a) heading: "### (a) Full-text keyword hits (FTS5, porter-stemmed)". Variant handling is consistent with it — distinct spellings that do not share a stem are both listed ("marihuana OR marijuana"), and §6 item 5 treats the stem-equivalent pair as one: "Do not search bare `drug`, `drugs`, or `smuggling` (1,572 hits…)".

`document_sources.citation_era` is a real column here (default 'unrecognized') and the memo uses `document_sources` heavily, yet never touches it (grep: no hit). All periodisation runs off `document_dates.date_iso` — §10: "sum(d.date_iso<'1970-01-01')" — and §9 states the choice: "Dates are document dates from `document_dates`, not publication dates." Eras are inferred from file-number form instead ("`341.9` | the 1950–63 Central Files narcotics class", "`SOC 11-5` | the 1963–73 subject-numeric narcotics class").

The archival table in §2(d) is labelled with its single source — "`document_sources.raw_text` / `decimal_class`" — and every archival query in §10 and §6 step 2 hits `document_sources` only. `external_citations` never appears in the memo (grep: no hit), so no combined count exists.

§2(a) shows the FTS query inline and §10 ("How to reproduce every number here") gives seven runnable statements. I ran them all: 1676/1087/51 hits, 1016 subject union, 150 for `File No. 774`, 268/7 for 811.114, 64632 for the 1948–60 window, and the full decade table — every figure reproduced exactly. (Gap noted: no code for §7's compilation walk — "(c) requires walking `volume_structures.structure_json`" — nor for §8's cross-check or §4's phrase counts.)

Proportions carry denominators throughout: §3 "**268 documents, of which only 7** mention any narcotics term and 216 mention liquor"; "`893.114` (China) is 44/46 narcotics"; "(48/51, 28/31, 19/28, 9/9, 8/8, 7/8)"; §4 "**82 subject-tagged documents**, against 64,632 corpus documents in the window (0.13%, versus 0.44% for 1906–47)" — the one percentage given is accompanied by both denominators. §9 "**428 documents of which 426** fall in its later era bucket."

Empty results are stated and paired with a positive check that the window could return rows: §1 "**Not one document dated 1948–1960 sits in a narcotics-titled compilation** — against 64,632 corpus documents dated in that window", with §10's `select count(*) from document_dates where date_iso between '1948-01-01' and '1960-12-31';  # 64632` proving the date range is populated (I re-ran it: 64632). Also §3(ii) "`511.4C1` (7 docs) … **liquor traffic in Africa, zero narcotics mentions**" — a zero reported against a non-empty base.

§9 flags thin results as artefacts of the indexing rather than the record: "The subject taxonomy is the Office of the Historian's, applied unevenly. Its density is much higher in modern volumes. **A pre-1970 volume being lightly tagged is weak evidence of absence.**" §1 does the same for the biggest negative finding ("a hole in FRUS's selection, not in the archive"), and §7's Turkey row is marked "**only ~1 doc is on narcotics; treat this row as inflated**".

§3 runs both against the decimal-class instrument in one pass and reports both: negatives — "`811.114` (the United States file) holds **268 documents, of which only 7 mention any narcotics term**" and "`511.4C1` (7 docs) … **zero narcotics mentions**"; positives — "By contrast `893.114` (China) is 44/46 narcotics" and "All the `511.4A*` sub-files and `511.4R1` are genuinely narcotics (48/51, 28/31, 19/28, 9/9, 8/8, 7/8)". §10 ships the 811.114 control query, which I re-ran (268|7).

§2(a) names the surface and tokenizer in its heading — "Full-text keyword hits (FTS5, porter-stemmed)" — and §9 states what was *not* scanned: "**I did not open the TEI XML.** Everything above is from the SQLite index and the bundled JSON. If a compilation heading is malformed in the XML, my §7 table inherits the error." (It does not enumerate which FTS columns are indexed, so header/source-note hits are silently included in "mention" counts.)

Eleven variants in one MATCH — "narcotic OR narcotics OR opium OR cocaine OR morphine OR heroin OR marihuana OR marijuana OR cannabis OR hashish OR \"dangerous drugs\"" — and the split is reported per term in §2(b): "Opium (1,016), Narcotics (631), Heroin (175), Narcotics control (168), Cocaine (100), Morphine (99), Narcotics traffic (69), Drug industry (8)" (I verified all eight df values against document-subject-index.json — exact). §6 item 4 gives per-phrase counts, and §3(ii) reports orthographic variants: "`511.4Al` and `511.4a6` appear alongside `511.4A1`/`511.4A6`, and the pre-WWII volumes print the class with spaces (`511.4 A 2/31b`)".

§9 states the choice outright: "**Dates are document dates from `document_dates`, not publication dates.**" The decade table in §2(a) is built as "`substr(date_iso,1,3)||'0s'`" and every period claim joins `document_dates`; I reproduced the decade table exactly. Volume years are used only as volume labels, never as the period axis.

`grep -niE "ed2|second edition"` over the memo returns nothing — the fold is neither applied nor checked-and-dismissed. It is live in this period: the DB holds `frus1951-54IranEd2`, which contributes 2 documents to the memo's own keyword MATCH and 2 to its eight-id subject union, both inside the pre-1970 window and both counted twice against their first-edition twins.

§2(d) "Archival provenance — the Department's own file classes" is a whole measure built from where the documents came from — "`document_sources.raw_text` / `decimal_class` … the State Department filed narcotics under identifiable numbers and FRUS prints the file number in the source note" — with a six-row table: `774/…` 1906–10 Numerical File (150), `511.4A*`/`511.4R1` (~158), `500.C1197` League Advisory Committee (33), `NNN.114 Narcotics/…` (58), `341.9` (13), `SOC 11-5` (52). I reproduced the 774 count (150) and the 811.114 control (268/7).

The footnote channel is never opened: `external_citations` does not appear anywhere in the memo (grep: no hit), and §6's search plan lists only `document_sources.raw_text LIKE …`, the subject union and full-text phrases. The channel is applicable and populated — `external_citations` holds 49,687 rows, 156 of them on documents matching the memo's own narcotics MATCH, resolving to Nixon Presidential Materials/NSC Files (29), Carter Library/National Security Affairs (29), Department of State lot 54 D 423 (5) and others. The one thing the memo calls a footnote in §5 ("The FRUS editorial note attached to it") is in fact the document's `source_note`, i.e. the channel it had already used.

Only one archival channel is used and it is named at the point of counting — §2(d) heading "`document_sources.raw_text` / `decimal_class`" — and §6 step 2 repeats the channel for the reader ("`document_sources.raw_text LIKE '%Narcotics/%'`…"). No figure anywhere adds a source-note count to a footnote-citation count, since the latter is never computed.

§2(d): "`decimal-class-labels.json` (parsed from NARA's *Classification of Correspondence, August 1910 – December 1949*) gives subject suffix `114` = **\"Traffic in liquors and habit-forming drugs\"** under class 8, Internal Affairs of States, and class 5 = \"Congresses and Conferences.\"" I opened the bundled artifact: schedule 0's `subjects['8']['114']` is exactly "Traffic in liquors and habit-forming drugs", `classes['8']` is "Internal Affairs of States", `classes['5']` is "Congresses and Conferences", and `source` is "RG 59 Department of State Classification of Correspondence, August 1910 – December 1949". §5 names a concrete target verbatim: "`RG 59, Central Files 1960–63, 341.9/1–1961`" — record group, series and file number. Confirmed against the DB: frus1961-63v25/d326's source_note reads "National Archives and Records Administration, RG 59, Central Files 1960–63, 341.9/1–1961". a4.notes:
Note: the rubric's table lists 25 rows (C1–C2, I1–I3, E1–E3, T1–T3, R1–R4, S1–S5, A1–A5) though its heading says 24; I scored all 25 as written. Compliance = 21/24 = 0.875 over scorable items.

VERIFICATION. I independently re-ran every query in §10 against frus-copy.db and opened the bundled JSON the memo cites. Everything reproduced: 1,676 FTS hits / 1,087 pre-1970 / 51 undated; 1,016 subject union pre-1970; 150 for `File No. 774`; 268 documents at `811.114` of which 7 match narcotics terms; 64,632 documents dated 1948–60; the full decade table (26/33/64/54/161/142/136/187/132/78/74/460) matched cell for cell. All eight subject-id document-frequencies matched document-subject-index.json exactly, as did the class-8 `114` gloss, classes 5 and 8, and the country numbers in decimal-class-labels.json. Three spot-checked document citations (frus1908/d72 with File No. 774/197A, frus1887/d148 Bayard→Denby, frus1906p1/d332) are all correct, and the §5 quotation is word-for-word the stored source note. Two trivial slips found: "211 distinct volumes" is 213 pre-1970 (272 for all hits), and my own independent walk of volume_structures found 47 narcotics-titled sections in 37 volumes against the memo's 40/35, including two the §7 table omits (frus1936v01 Suppression conference, frus1944v05). Neither affects an item.

THE THREE FAILURES, and they are structural rather than sloppy.

A2 is the substantive one. The memo builds a serious archival measure out of one channel — `document_sources`, where the printed document came from — and never opens the other, `external_citations`, where the editors' footnotes point. That table is not empty for this topic (156 rows joined to the memo's own MATCH, naming Nixon NSC Files, Carter NSA files, Kennedy NSF and State lot 54 D 423), and §6's search plan omits it too, so a reader following the memo would never find it. Compounding this, §5 calls a `source_note` "The FRUS editorial note attached to it" — the memo appears not to distinguish the two channels conceptually, which is exactly what A2 exists to test. A3 still passes because only one channel was counted and it was labelled; there was nothing to sum.

E1: not one figure in the memo excludes or discloses apparatus. 8,468 editorial notes and 1,012 front-matter rows sit inside the 316,839 denominator, the 64,632 window and the 1,676 hits with no filter and no statement. §9's remark about d336/d342 is a correct local observation (both are indeed is_editorial_note=1) but covers two rows in one chapter, not the counting policy.

S5: the Ed2 fold is unmentioned and live — frus1951-54IranEd2 double-counts 2 documents into both the keyword and subject measures inside the memo's own period.

WHERE I WAS CLOSE TO MARKING DOWN BUT DID NOT.
